fixes.explanation: Yes, baker. God says, "…its sound will be heard when he enters or exits the sanctuary before the LORD…" (Exodus 28:35). Around the lower hem, gold bells alternate with pomegranates (Exodus 28:33, 34). So that sound goes with Aaron every time he walks in or out.

Camp is a fair guess, baker, but it isn't the word in the verse. God says, "…its sound will be heard when he enters or exits the sanctuary before the LORD…" (Exodus 28:35). The verse is about Aaron going in and out of the sanctuary. That's the word to remember.

That's it, baker. God tells Moses to make a plate of pure gold and engrave on it "…as on a seal: HOLY TO THE LORD." (Exodus 28:36). A blue cord mounts it on the front of the turban (Exodus 28:37). It's worn on Aaron's forehead (Exodus 28:38).

problems.problem: It uses a dash. No em dashes or en dashes.
It reuses a line from the Prep cards word for word.
The soundtrack joke makes the holy priestly robe the subject of the joke.
The comparison to aiming for a big place does not connect to entering or exiting the sanctuary, so the joke lacks a clear logic.
The jealousy joke uses the holy gold plate and its engraved words as the subject of the joke.
